AXIS: the autonomy number. Today an ordinary row books a full model grading session, so every task
is paid for twice — once to make it, once to re-derive it. Make the cheap grade the DEFAULT rather
than the opt-in, and the same token budget buys roughly twice the shipped work.

## The measurement that forced this (main, 2026-09-19)

Summed `message.usage` across every seat's Claude Code transcripts, last 7 days, QUOTA basis
(input + output + cache-write + cache-read):

    quinn (grader)  16,845 msgs   2,318.8M quota tokens
    dev   (maker)   15,998 msgs   2,307.0M quota tokens

**The single grader out-burns the maker whose work it grades, by 0.5%.** 97.8% of quinn's burn is
cache-read — context re-sent, not thinking. lodar, 2026-09-19 12:11Z: *"quinn basically does the
devs burn and even more"*, *"we cant afford to double burn the same task"*, *"verifier should be
super token efficient"*.

Do NOT re-derive this from `5dive account usage`. That reports percentage of a rolling limit, it
resets (a fresh window reads ~0% regardless of history), and it is per ACCOUNT not per seat —
chemmonitor carries main, quinn, olivia and ops together. I got this wrong that way first. The
transcripts are the only per-seat ledger on the box.

## What already exists and is not the gap

`--review=check` grades a row with a command and spends ZERO model tokens. `verify-small` (raised
25 -> 150 today) closes a small non-blast-radius delivery with no grader at all. DIVE-4576's result
template already forces CHANGED / CHECKED / DELIVERED-SHA / CI / CRITERIA so a grader re-runs a
claim instead of re-investigating a diff.

**The gap is that `--review=temp` is still the default for an ordinary row.** `check` is not trusted
as a default because nothing proves the command it runs would actually FAIL on a broken tree — a
grade command that passes on any tree is not a grade.

## THE ASK — a mandatory mutant arm on `--review=check`

`--review=check` gains `--mutant=<cmd>` (or an equivalent). At delivery, from a clean checkout at
the delivered sha, the grader runs the check BOTH ways:

1. apply -> the check must PASS;
2. revert the diff -> the check must FAIL.

A check that passes on the reverted tree is not evidence and the delivery is REJECTED with that as
the finding. This is the cheapest independent verification there is and it does not need to
understand the code.

Once that exists, `check` can become the default for any row that can name a grade command, and a
model grading session becomes the exception — bought deliberately with `--verify`, or triggered by
the blast-radius paths, not spent by default.

## ACCEPTANCE

1. `task add --review=check` accepts a mutant command and refuses `--review=check` without one
   (or documents the audited escape for a row that genuinely cannot have one).
2. The grader runs both arms from a clean checkout at the delivered sha and records both results
   on the row. Revert-passes -> reject.
3. A test proves the reject fires: a deliberately vacuous check command (e.g. `true`) is rejected.
4. The default-selection logic in `task add` is updated, and `task --help` states the new default.
5. No change to the blast-radius path fence — those rows keep their model grade at any size.

## Not in scope, deliberately

luca's other proposals (a `--scope=<paths>` fence, a `--review=rubric` cheap-model mode, grading in
the maker's worktree instead of a fresh clone, per-maker trust sampling) are real but separate. This
row is the one that unblocks the default change; the rest are only worth their own rows once this
lands and we can measure what is left. Source doc: claude-luca, 2026-09-19,
"Making an independent verifier cheap".

## SCOPE WIDENED 2026-09-19 12:18Z — this row now carries ALL FOUR verifier-cost changes

lodar, 12:17Z: *"can you merge those in one task or not?"* — yes, and it is the right call. DIVE-4624,
DIVE-4625 and DIVE-4626 are CANCELLED into this row. Four rows would have booked four grader
sessions to ship a fix for the cost of grader sessions, and all four touch the same code path.
One make, one PR, one grade.

Ship them as separable commits in that PR. Stage 1 is the keystone — if the pass runs long,
deliver 1+2 and say so; do NOT deliver a half-done stage.

### STAGE 1 (keystone) — the mutant arm. As specified in the body above.

### STAGE 2 — the grading prompt is the claim block + diff (was DIVE-4625)
**This is the one that attacks the measured number.** 97.8% of quinn's burn is cache-read, ~135k
re-sent per message across 16,845 messages. The two largest avoidable things in that context are
the row's narrative body (ours run 4,000 words of superseded prior-pass findings — this very body
is an example) and the maker's transcript, which also anchors the verdict to the maker's framing.

## The ask

The grading prompt is assembled from a fixed, bounded set:

- the acceptance criteria,
- the delivery claim block (DIVE-4576's CHANGED / CHECKED / DELIVERED-SHA / CI / CRITERIA),
- `git diff` at the delivered sha,
- the commands named in CHECKED, and their output.

**Not** the row's narrative body, **not** the maker's transcript, **not** the routing history. If a
grader needs something from the body it asks for it explicitly — that turns an always-paid cost into
a rarely-paid one.

## ACCEPTANCE

## ACCEPTANCE

1. Grade the same row before and after; report the QUOTA-token delta and the prompt size delta.
2. A row with a 4,000-word body produces a grading prompt that does not contain it.
3. The verdict quality is unchanged on a set of rows with known outcomes — include at least one row
   that SHOULD reject, and show it still rejects.

### STAGE 3 — grade in the maker's worktree at the delivered sha (was DIVE-4624)
## The ask

The grader reads the MAKER'S tree at the delivered sha instead of building its own: a git worktree
at that sha, or `sudo -u <maker>` into the maker's checkout the way the existing grade helper
already does. It then runs the commands the delivery named in CHECKED, in that tree.

Two properties must survive, and they are the reason this is a row and not a one-liner:

1. **The sha is still pinned.** Reading the maker's worktree must not become reading whatever the
   maker has uncommitted. Verify HEAD equals the delivered sha and the tree is clean before
   grading, and REJECT with that as the finding if it is not.
2. **Independence of evidence is preserved.** The maker must not be able to make a check pass by
   editing the tree under the grader mid-grade. Detach to a worktree at the sha rather than reading
   the live checkout, or snapshot and compare.

## ACCEPTANCE

1. A grade runs without cloning or installing — show the before/after wall time and the before/after
   QUOTA tokens for the same row graded both ways.
2. A dirty or wrong-sha tree is refused, with a test proving the refusal fires.
3. The maker cannot mutate the graded tree during the grade; name the mechanism that stops it.

### STAGE 4 — the cheap fixed-question rubric (was DIVE-4626)
## The ask

`--review=rubric`: a cheap-model (sonnet or haiku, low effort) pass over the diff and the claim
block, answering a FIXED question set yes/no, each answer quoting the line it rests on:

1. Does a test actually exercise the change?
2. Is a mutant arm present — does something go red on the reverted tree?
3. Is any file touched outside the row's stated scope?
4. Does the changelog / result claim match the diff?
5. Is there a secret or a real identifier in the diff?
6. Does any CHECKED claim contradict what the diff shows?

Escalate to a full grading session ONLY on a flag, or on a blast-radius path (scheduler, task store,
credentials, deploy, shared libs, sudo policy, systemd, schema, provisioning), or on `--verify`.
Otherwise the rubric's clean pass IS the grade.

Note item 3 above doubles as luca's scope fence (his item 3) — the row states its paths and a file
outside them is a finding. Implement it here rather than as its own row.

## Why a fixed question set and not "review this diff"

## ACCEPTANCE

1. `task add --review=rubric` exists and `task --help` states what it does and what it costs.
2. On a corpus of already-graded rows the rubric's flag/no-flag call matches the recorded verdict;
   report the confusion matrix, and treat a missed reject as a blocker, not a footnote.
3. Report QUOTA tokens per rubric pass against the per-session-grade baseline.
4. Blast-radius paths still take the full grade at any size.

## Deliberately NOT in this row

### STILL NOT IN SCOPE
luca item 2 (structured delivery refused when unverifiable) already exists as DIVE-4576's template.
luca item 6 (per-maker trust sampling) depends on stages 1 and 4 landing — file it after, not now.

### What shipped against the five acceptance criteria

1. `--review=check` now REFUSES without `--mutant=<cmd>`; the audited escape is
   `--no-mutant="<reason>"`, stored as `none: <reason>` in the new nullable `mutant_command`
   column (additive migration, positive-controlled on a live store: absent under origin/main's
   `tasks_db_init`, present after the new tree migrates the SAME database).
2. At delivery both arms run from a CLEAN CHECKOUT at the delivered sha
   (`_task_check_control_arms`, src/task/delivery.sh): arm A as delivered must PASS, arm B
   after the mutant must FAIL. Both are recorded on the row — carried into the grade record as
   the verifier's prose, so they land in the cell the board and the merge owner already read.
   Revert-passes -> `policy_refuse deliver-check-vacuous`, no handoff, no spawn request.
3. `tests/task_check_mutant_arm_unit.sh` — 37/37 green. The criterion-3 arm files a row with
   `--verify=true --mutant=true` and asserts the DELIVERY is refused with spawn_count 0.
   21 of 35 arms RED on the pre-fix tree (origin/main + this harness only).
4. Default-selection: a row that resolves to `temp` is now told on its created line what it
   would take to be command-graded instead, and `task --help` states check as the preferred
   lane with both flags documented.
5. Blast-radius path fence untouched.

### Decisions taken, with the alternatives NOT taken (nothing here was a question for a human)

- **A bare `--verify=<cmd>` still resolves to `check` and still delivers.** Alternative
  considered and rejected: refuse it, or re-route it to a grader session. Both re-introduce, on
  every legacy command-graded row at once, exactly the burn this row exists to remove. The gap
  is RECORDED instead ("control: NONE RECORDED" on the row, plus a warn), so an uncontrolled
  grade is countable rather than silently equal to a proven one.
- **The revert arm is a NAMED mutant command, not an automatic reverse-diff.** An automatic
  revert needs the PR base, and reverting everything (including the new test) makes the check
  fail for want of a file — a green control arm that proves nothing. The ASK offers
  `--mutant=<cmd>` "or an equivalent"; this is the honest equivalent.
- **Arm B does NOT go through `cmd_task_verify`**, which is the opposite of the choice
  DIVE-4576 made one function above, deliberately: arm B's pass/fail is INVERTED, so the verb
  that records grades would stamp a FAIL on a row whose control just worked. The primary grade
  still goes through it, unchanged.
- **Arm A red is its own refusal class** (`deliver-check-red-at-sha`), not folded into the
  vacuity finding: they are different defects (the pushed tree is missing something vs the
  check is meaningless) and a merge owner reading the row needs to know which.

### Residuals I am signing, not hiding

- A check or mutant naming the maker's tree by ABSOLUTE PATH reaches around the clean checkout
  and reads the dirty files anyway. Detected and warned, not refused — the path may
  legitimately be a fixture outside the repo.
- A clean checkout has no installed dependencies, so a repo whose check needs `npm ci` /
  `bun install` must either include that in the check command or take `--no-mutant=<reason>`.
  Untested beyond the bash-only case; 5dive-cli's own harnesses need no install.
- Each arm is capped at `FIVEDIVE_CONTROL_ARM_TIMEOUT` (default 900s) when `timeout` exists; a
  box without coreutils `timeout` runs the arms uncapped.
- Neighbour harnesses updated for the new requirement: `task_review_mode_unit` 47/0 (+1 arm for
  the new refusal), `task_delivery_evidence_unit` 53/0 — its command-graded fixtures take the
  audited waiver because their check command is literally `true`, and its mutation sed was
  re-anchored off the now-6-argument call (the old sed matched nothing and self-reported).
  `graded_merge_hold_dispatch_unit` 32/0, `verify_command_grade_stamps_sha_unit` 29/0.
- CI has not run: nothing is pushed yet.
